title: Гражданин мира и выход на пробежку  (Citizen of the World and Heading Out to Jog)

segments.t: Amused by Kostya's predicament, Max cheerfully declares that he does not mind Rodion staying at the apartment—so long as Rodion sleeps in Kostya and Nastya's room. The next morning in the park, Chef Barinov shows up in a brand-new tracksuit and surprises Elena by actually appearing for their morning jog.
Пускай остается у нас.
Мы с Максом не против.
А ты убирай, в какой комнате будешь жить?
С вами.
Родион Сергеевич.
Прошу прощения.
Я гражданин мира, мне нечего скрывать.
Доброе утро.
Даже не думал, что вы придете.
Ну что, побежали?
Еще умолять будете, чтобы я остановился.
Да ладно вам.
Ну, вперед.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Пускай остается у нас.
'Let him stay here with us.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'let' and finishing on 'us'.
Мы с Максом не против.
'Max and I have no objection.' In Russian, the idea of 'we' flows naturally into 'against' without extra filler words.
А ты убирай, в какой комнате будешь жить?
'So pick which room you are going to sleep in?' Rodion raises the pitch on 'to live' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Max answers right away.
С вами.
'In the room with you two.' The grammar packs 'with' and 'with you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Родион Сергеевич.
'Rodion Sergeyevich.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Rodion' and finishing on 'Sergeyevich'.
Прошу прощения.
'I beg your pardon.' Rodion brings out the contrast between 'beg' and 'forgiveness' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
Я гражданин мира, мне нечего скрывать.
'I am a citizen of the world, I have nothing to hide.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'to hide' in spoken Russian.
Доброе утро.
'Good morning.' Notice how Russian expresses 'kind' and 'morning' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Даже не думал, что вы придете.
'I did not even think that you would actually show up.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'even' and finishing on 'to come'. Max answers right away.
Ну что, побежали?
'Well then, shall we run?' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'to start running' covers a group or the polite 'you'.
Еще умолять будете, чтобы я остановился.
'You will be begging me to stop before long.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'else' and finishing on 'stopped'.
Да ладно вам.
'Oh, come on now.' Rodion chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'for you' to keep a polite distance. Max answers right away.
Ну, вперед.
'All right, forward march.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'ahead of'. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
